sources.entry: A news aggregator, also termed a feed aggregator, feed reader, news reader, RSS reader, is an application that aggregates web content such as newspapers/blogs/vlogs/podcasts in one location for easy viewing.

summary.name: News aggregator
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing news aggregators (feed readers), client software or web applications that collect online newspapers, blogs, podcasts and vlogs in one place.
keywords: subscribe to blogs in one place
use_cases: Following many blogs and news sites in one view
Subscribing to podcasts and downloading episodes automatically
Filtering large volumes of feed articles by keyword
Aggregating community blogs with planet-style sites
summary.what_it_does: The page explains that news aggregators are client software or web applications that consolidate feeds (mainly RSS, Atom, and RDF/XML) so users see only new or updated items from many sites. Feed readers can check for updates at user-set intervals, and many let users tag feeds with keywords to sort and filter articles. Podcast-capable aggregators can download media files and sync them to portable players. The article also covers news aggregation websites such as Google News, social news aggregators, media-bias-aware aggregators, and broadcatching of BitTorrent files via RSS.
notable: Covers the history of RSS, from its 1999 introduction by Netscape to its adoption by major browsers in 2005
Describes web-based versus desktop feed readers and their trade-offs
Notes that Google Reader's shutdown led some to predict RSS's death, but Feedly's paid user base grew substantially by 2015
caveats: Article is a general encyclopedia overview, not a page for a single tool
Page is flagged as having multiple issues and some claims lack citations
Reflects facts as of around 2015 in places
